title: Glutathione Synthesis
pm_id: BRS2-FM2-PM6
mission: >-
  Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon
  metabolism.
parent_fm: BRS2(FM2)
parent_brs: BRS2
evidence_status: stage-2b-dietary-addressability
summary: >-
  Cells assemble glutathione, the main intracellular thiol, in two ATP-dependent steps. Glutamate–cysteine
  ligase joins glutamate and cysteine, then glutathione synthetase adds glycine. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet
  slowed whole-blood synthesis in healthy young men. Combined precursor supplements raised erythrocyte
  synthesis in older adults. These tracer studies measured synthesis in blood cells, not in the brain.
key_constraints:
  - BRS2(KC2) - Methionine–Cysteine Sulfur Amino Acid Pool
pm_kc_relationships:
  - relationship_id: BRS2-FM2-PM6-KCR-1
    dietary_input: false
    dietary_input_note: >-
      Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its
      separately admitted PM input atoms.
    kc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    ikc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    pm_biological_role: >-
      Removing methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis, and removing
      cysteine alone did not when methionine stayed adequate. That is the sulfur-amino-acid provision
      relationship already recorded for cysteine and methionine.
    evidence_source:
      finding_ids:
        - PM6-F1
        - PM6-F2
      citation_keys:
        - lyons_glutathione_2000
        - misra_human_gcl_1998
        - courtney_martin_cysteine_2008
    evidence_limitation: >-
      Lyons used a 10-day amino-acid formula that removed both methionine and cysteine in healthy young men,
      and whole-blood glutathione concentration was maintained. Courtney-Martin kept methionine adequate and
      found that removing cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men. Neither study identifies
      a bottleneck beyond those provision relationships. This is not neuronal synthesis, ordinary mixed-diet
      advice, or a benefit from increasing an adequate intake.
    presentation_review:
      disposition: consolidated as duplicate
      compared_records:
        3.1.1:
          - PM6-DIT-1
          - PM6-DIT-9
        3.1.2: []
        '3.2': []
      retained_record_ids:
        - PM6-DIT-1
        - PM6-DIT-9
        - BRS2-FM2-PM6-KCR-1
      rationale: >-
        Sulfur-amino-acid provision sustaining glutathione synthesis is cysteine as the direct assembly
        substrate and methionine as its precursor. A resource-dependency label and a KC2 origin tag do not
        create a further biological job. Lyons supplies the combined-depletion bound and Courtney-Martin the
        adequate-methionine bound. No additional competition, allocation, or other bottleneck was measured.
    relationship_type: conditional-constraint
    legacy_relationship_mode: constrained-by
    public_disclosure: consolidated-as-duplicate

  - kc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    ikc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    arm_id: methionine-cysteine-sulfur-amino-acid-pool
    applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains glutathione synthesis capacity.
    disposition: established
    applicability_mode: conditional-constraint
    established_links:
      - Glutamate-cysteine ligase uses cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine (PM6-F1).
      - >-
        A diet containing neither methionine nor cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione fractional and
        absolute synthesis in healthy young men, while glycine intake was not reduced (PM6-F2).
      - >-
        With methionine held at an adequate intake, cysteine intakes from zero upward did not change
        erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in young men (PM6-F2).
    inferred_links:
      - Ordinary mixed diets are commonly short of this pool.
      - The same synthesis-rate change occurs in neurons or in clinical populations.
    evidence_source:
      finding_ids:
        - PM6-F1
        - PM6-F2
      citation_keys:
        - lyons_glutathione_2000
        - misra_human_gcl_1998
        - courtney_martin_cysteine_2008
    rationale: >-
      KC2 applicability stays established because these sulfur-amino-acid studies bear on glutathione
      synthesis. The public disclosure is consolidated as a duplicate of PM6-DIT-1 and PM6-DIT-9. Lyons is
      combined depletion. Courtney-Martin is the adequate-methionine boundary. Neither study measures a
      competition, allocation, or other bottleneck beyond that provision.
    legacy_applicability_mode: constrained-by
cofactors:

intervention_dominance: Diet-Dominant
intervention_breakdown: Food-State Dominant
timing_specific: 'No'
dose_sensitivity: >-

  erythrocyte synthesis in older adults only; that is not general dietary advice. Selenium and riboflavin are
  not synthesis requirements.

    description_finding_id: PM6-F1
scientific_findings_intro: >-
  Human tracer studies show context-dependent substrate responsiveness. Removing methionine and cysteine
  together reduced whole-blood glutathione synthesis, whereas removing cysteine with methionine kept adequate
  did not reduce erythrocyte synthesis in young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) In older adults with
  lower baseline synthesis, combined N-acetylcysteine and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte
  synthesis. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These contrasts support provision under defined conditions, not universal
  dietary cysteine limitation; blood-cell measurements do not establish neuronal synthesis or clinical
  benefit.
scientific_findings:
  - id: PM6-F1
    finding_label: Two ATP-dependent enzymes assemble glutathione
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: true
    finding_summary: >-
      Glutamate-cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine using ATP. Glutathione synthetase then adds
      glycine, again using ATP, and binds magnesium. Selenium-dependent peroxidase activity and
      riboflavin-derived FAD in glutathione reductase are not part of these assembly reactions.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      Glutamate, cysteine, glycine and ATP are the assembly substrates. Magnesium participates in the second
      enzyme. ATP and magnesium are intracellular biochemical requirements, not dietary levers. Selenium and
      riboflavin support later use and recycling of glutathione.
    finding_statement: >-
      Glutathione synthesis requires ATP-dependent formation of γ-glutamylcysteine from glutamate and
      cysteine, followed by ATP-dependent addition of glycine, and does not use selenium or riboflavin as
      synthesis substrates.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      Reviewed catalytic annotation of purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase records ATP-dependent ligation
      of L-glutamate and L-cysteine as the first step. Human glutathione synthetase structural work records
      ATP-dependent addition of glycine and one bound magnesium ion per subunit as the second step. Together
      they define the assembly boundary. Human glutathione peroxidase uses an active-site selenocysteine to
      reduce peroxides with glutathione already formed, and glutathione reductase binds FAD while reducing
      glutathione disulfide. Those enzymes consume or restore glutathione; they do not assemble it.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The enzyme evidence is purified protein and structure, not intact human flux. A lower cysteine Km on the
      first enzyme does not prove that ordinary diets are cysteine-limited. Magnesium binding does not show
      that magnesium intake changes synthesis. The dietary review that groups selenium and riboflavin with
      glutathione support does not move those cofactors into the assembly reactions.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Misra and Griffith (1998)
        citation_key: misra_human_gcl_1998
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#misra_human_gcl_1998
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase catalyses ATP-dependent ligation of L-glutamate and
          L-cysteine, the first step of glutathione biosynthesis.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Expression and purification of human gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase, with catalytic constants
            recorded in the reviewed human GCLC entry that cites this paper.
          population: Purified human enzyme; no human participants.
          result: >-
            The reaction consumes L-glutamate, L-cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine, ADP and
            phosphate. The cited annotation reports Km values of 0.1 mM for L-cysteine, 1.8 mM for L-glutamate
            and 0.4 mM for ATP.
          effect_magnitude: Purified-enzyme Km values only; no human synthesis-rate effect.
          evidence_summary: >-
            Direct human-enzyme evidence for the first ATP-dependent assembly step and its amino-acid and ATP
            substrates.
          limitations: >-
            In-vitro constants do not establish in-vivo limitation, dietary responsiveness, tissue differences
            or clinical effects.
      - label: Polekhina et al. (1999)
        citation_key: polekhina_gss_1999
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#polekhina_gss_1999
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Human glutathione synthetase produces glutathione from γ-glutamylcysteine and glycine in an
          ATP-dependent reaction and binds one magnesium ion per subunit.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Crystal structure of human glutathione synthetase at 2.10 Å in complex with ADP and glutathione,
            with catalytic and cofactor annotation.
          population: Crystallised human glutathione synthetase; no human participants.
          result: >-
            The structure and catalytic annotation place glycine and ATP in the second assembly step and
            record one Mg2+ ion bound per subunit.
          effect_magnitude: 2.10 Å structure; no physiological effect size.
          evidence_summary: Direct structural evidence for the second ATP-dependent step and its magnesium ion.
          limitations: >-
            A product-bound structure establishes catalytic participants, not dietary dose response or in-vivo
            flux.
    connected_supportive_evidence:
      - label: Minich et al. (2019)
        citation_key: minich_glutathione_2019
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#minich_glutathione_2019
        data_level: Mechanistic
        why_relevant: >-
          Reviews dietary nutrients discussed for glutathione support, including sulfur amino acids, selenium

        why_excluded: >-
          It is a narrative review and does not itself measure the ligase reactions, ATP use, or separation of
          assembly from peroxidase and reductase cofactors.
      - label: Mullenbach et al. (1987)
        citation_key: mullenbach_gpx_selenocysteine_1987
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#mullenbach_gpx_selenocysteine_1987
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        why_relevant: >-
          Shows that human glutathione peroxidase encodes an active-site selenocysteine, so selenium belongs

        why_excluded: >-
          Peroxidase activity consumes glutathione. It is not a substrate or cofactor of either assembly

      - label: Karplus and Schulz (1989)
        citation_key: karplus_glutathione_reductase_1989
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#karplus_glutathione_reductase_1989

        why_relevant: >-
          Glutathione reductase structures show bound FAD, the riboflavin-derived cofactor, at the enzyme that

        why_excluded: >-

          glutamate-cysteine ligase or glutathione synthetase.
  - id: PM6-F2
    finding_label: Blood-cell synthesis responds only under defined substrate conditions
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: true
    finding_summary: >-
      Removing both methionine and cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young men.
      Combined cysteine-precursor and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. A
      methionine-adequate diet without cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      Substrate supply can change blood-cell synthesis in these specific conditions. That does not mean every
      ordinary diet is cysteine-limited, and the older-adult result is a supplemental precursor plus glycine,
      not a food prescription.
    finding_statement: >-
      Human blood-cell glutathione synthesis can slow when dietary methionine and cysteine are both removed
      and can rise in older adults after combined cysteine and glycine precursor supplementation, whereas a
      methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not limit erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      Three human tracer studies set the ceiling. In seven healthy young men, a 10-day amino-acid diet with
      methionine and cysteine removed lowered whole-blood fractional synthesis from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13
      per day and lowered absolute synthesis by about 23%, while concentration stayed near 1.2 mM and glycine
      intake was not reduced. In eight older adults compared with eight younger adults, erythrocyte
      glutathione synthesis and concentration were lower, and two weeks of cysteine plus glycine precursor
      supplementation raised fractional synthesis by 78.8% and absolute synthesis by 230.9%. The cysteine
      source in that protocol is N-acetylcysteine, given with glycine. In four young men, cysteine intakes
      from zero to 40 mg/kg/day did not change erythrocyte synthesis when methionine was held at 14 mg/kg/day.
      Synthesis is therefore substrate-responsive under defined restrictions, not universally limited by
      dietary cysteine.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an
      experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required
      combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial,
      and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation.
      Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Lyons et al. (2000)
        citation_key: lyons_glutathione_2000
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#lyons_glutathione_2000
        data_level: Human Mechanistic
        exposure_context: dietary
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          A sulfur-amino-acid-free amino-acid diet slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young
          men without lowering glutathione concentration.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Randomised crossover of two 10-day L-amino-acid diets, adequate versus methionine and cysteine
            both set to zero, with a primed intravenous L-[1-13C]cysteine infusion on day 10.
          population: Seven healthy men, age 24 ± 6 years.
          result: >-
            Fractional synthesis fell from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day (P < 0.01). Absolute synthesis
            fell from 747 ± 216 to 578.6 ± 135 µmol/L/day (P < 0.05), about 23%. Whole-blood glutathione
            stayed about 1.2 mM (1,142 ± 243 versus 1,216 ± 162 µM). Glycine in the formula rose from 39.6 to
            75.1 mg/kg/day so nitrogen stayed constant; glutamic acid was unchanged.
          effect_magnitude: >-
            About a 23% lower absolute synthesis rate after 10 days without methionine and cysteine;
            concentration unchanged.
          evidence_summary: >-
            Direct human evidence that removing the shared sulfur-amino-acid supply slows whole-blood
            glutathione synthesis.
          limitations: >-
            Experimental formula, young men, short duration, whole blood rather than brain, and no clinical
            outcome. Glycine was increased, so the slowdown is not a glycine deficit.
      - label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
        citation_key: sekhar_glutathione_2011
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#sekhar_glutathione_2011
        data_level: Human Mechanistic
        exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Older adults had lower erythrocyte glutathione synthesis than younger adults, and two weeks of
          cysteine plus glycine precursor supplementation restored synthesis and concentration.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Stable-isotope erythrocyte glutathione kinetics before and after precursor supplementation.
            Cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine.
          population: Eight older adults restudied after supplementation, compared with eight younger adults.
          result: >-
            Before supplementation, older adults had lower erythrocyte glycine, cysteine, glutathione
            concentration, fractional synthesis (45.80 ± 5.69 versus 83.14 ± 6.43 %/day) and absolute
            synthesis (0.55 ± 0.12 versus 1.73 ± 0.16 mmol/L red cells per day). After two weeks, glutathione
            concentration was 94.6% higher, fractional synthesis 78.8% higher and absolute synthesis 230.9%
            higher, and plasma oxidative-stress markers were lower.
          effect_magnitude: >-
            Combined precursor supplementation in older adults: fractional synthesis +78.8% and absolute
            synthesis +230.9% from the deficient baseline.
          evidence_summary: >-
            Human evidence that combined supplemental cysteine precursor and glycine can raise erythrocyte
            glutathione synthesis when it is low in older adults.
          limitations: >-
            Small older-adult sample, erythrocyte pool, combined supplements, not ordinary food, not neuronal
            synthesis, and not an ADHD or recovery trial.
      - label: Courtney-Martin et al. (2008)
        citation_key: courtney_martin_cysteine_2008
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#courtney_martin_cysteine_2008
        data_level: Human Mechanistic
        exposure_context: dietary
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis did not change across cysteine intakes, including zero, when
          methionine intake was adequate.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Five graded cysteine intakes (0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg/kg/day) in random order with methionine
            fixed at 14 mg/kg/day and protein at 1 g/kg/day. Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis was measured
            after two days at each intake.
          population: Four healthy young adult men.
          result: >-
            Fractional and absolute erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and glutathione concentration did not
            change as cysteine intake increased. Urinary sulfate excretion rose with cysteine intake (r =
            0.92).
          effect_magnitude: No change in erythrocyte glutathione synthesis across the cysteine range tested.
          evidence_summary: >-
            Human evidence that dietary cysteine is not independently limiting for erythrocyte glutathione
            synthesis when methionine intake meets the protein requirement.
          limitations: >-
            Preliminary sample of four men, two-day adaptation, erythrocyte endpoint, and no neuronal or
            clinical outcome.
    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        Sekhar et al. (2011) is also used in PM6-F3 and PM6-F4 for the phenome boundary, and in PM6-IC1 for
        the measurement boundary. Those uses are not independent replications of the synthesis-rate result.
  - id: PM6-IC1
    finding_label: Blood-cell glutathione kinetics are not neuronal synthesis or clinical outcome
    presentation: interpretive-constraint
    finding_statement: >-
      Erythrocyte and whole-blood glutathione synthesis rates and concentrations do not measure neuronal
      glutathione synthesis, do not establish that every person is substrate-limited, and are not ADHD,
      recovery or stress-resilience outcomes.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      The human tracer studies measure incorporation of labelled cysteine or glycine into glutathione in whole
      blood or red cells. In the sulfur-amino-acid-free diet, synthesis slowed while concentration was
      maintained, so concentration is not a substitute for synthesis rate. None of the studies sampled brain
      glutathione synthesis or tested a recovery, stress or ADHD outcome. A paediatric ADHD study that found
      higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 did not measure glutathione.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      This constraint limits interpretation. It does not prove that neuronal synthesis is unrelated to
      substrate supply, and it does not reclassify the blood-cell synthesis results themselves.

      - label: Sekhar et al. (2011)

      - label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
        citation_key: lukovac_serum_2024
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#lukovac_serum_2024

          measured.

            Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 lower in the ADHD group. Glutathione synthesis was not an

          effect_magnitude: No glutathione concentration or synthesis rate was reported.
          evidence_summary: An ADHD biomarker association that does not measure this synthesis reaction.

    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        Lyons et al. (2000) and Sekhar et al. (2011) are primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2. PM6-IC1 uses

  - id: PM6-F3

## BRS2-2-6 - Glutathione Synthesis

(Assembling glutathione from glutamate, cysteine and glycine)

## 1. Mission & Overview + Dietary Levers

### Mission

Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.


**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Dominant

### Overview

Cells assemble glutathione, the main intracellular thiol, in two ATP-dependent steps. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine, then glutathione synthetase adds glycine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis in healthy young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) Combined precursor supplements raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These tracer studies measured synthesis in blood cells, not in the brain. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4)

- **Benefits:** Cells draw on this thiol to limit oxidative stress. In older adults, higher blood-cell synthesis after precursor supplements came with lower plasma oxidative-stress markers. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) That thiol is how sulfur amino acids from one-carbon metabolism stay connected to cellular antioxidant defence.
- **Implementation Notes:** Cysteine, methionine, glutamate, glycine, and N-acetylcysteine are the provision routes. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) A methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men, so these results do not set a routine dose. [[5]](#pm-ref-5)
- **Biological Relevance:** Clearing peroxides and recycling oxidised glutathione are separate from this assembly. [[8]](#pm-ref-8) [[9]](#pm-ref-9)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Glutathione formation is the point at which glutamate, cysteine and glycine become the cell's main low-molecular-weight thiol. The defining events are the two ATP-dependent assembly steps. Making the cysteine, and later using or recycling the glutathione, are separate processes.

<div class="brs-fm-hub-item" data-brs-fm-hub>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-shell">
<button type="button" class="brs-fm-hub-summary" aria-expanded="false">
<span class="brs-fm-hub-chevron" aria-hidden="true"></span>
<strong>Glutathione synthesis — mechanistic detail</strong>
</button>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-panel" hidden>

#### (Two ATP-dependent assembly steps)

Glutathione (GSH; γ-glutamylcysteinylglycine) is built in two steps that each use ATP (the cell's energy-carrying molecule). Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins the side-chain carboxyl of glutamate to cysteine, forming γ-glutamylcysteine (a two-amino-acid intermediate) [[1]](#pm-ref-1). Glutathione synthetase then adds glycine, and the human enzyme binds one magnesium ion per subunit [[2]](#pm-ref-2). The reviewed constants for the purified first enzyme give cysteine a lower Km (0.1 mM) than glutamate (1.8 mM) [[1]](#pm-ref-1). That biochemical preference is not the same thing as a universal dietary cysteine shortage.

#### (When human blood-cell synthesis changes)

In seven healthy young men, removing methionine and cysteine from an otherwise adequate amino-acid formula for 10 days lowered whole-blood fractional synthesis from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day and lowered absolute synthesis by about 23%, while glutathione concentration stayed near 1.2 mM. Glycine in that formula was increased, not reduced [[3]](#pm-ref-3). In older adults, erythrocyte synthesis was lower than in younger adults and rose after two weeks of a cysteine precursor, supplied as N-acetylcysteine, together with glycine [[4]](#pm-ref-4). When methionine was held at 14 mg/kg/day, cysteine intakes from zero to 40 mg/kg/day did not change erythrocyte synthesis in four young men [[5]](#pm-ref-5).

#### (What is outside the assembly reactions)

Selenium is part of glutathione peroxidase: human glutathione peroxidase uses an active-site selenocysteine and glutathione to reduce peroxides [[8]](#pm-ref-8). Riboflavin is relevant because glutathione reductase binds FAD, a riboflavin-derived cofactor, while it reduces oxidised glutathione back to the reduced form [[9]](#pm-ref-9). A dietary review groups these nutrients with glutathione support [[6]](#pm-ref-6). They act after glutathione has been made.

#### (Boundaries of the mechanism)

This reaction is glutathione assembly from glutamate, cysteine and glycine. Conversion of homocysteine to cysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway). Remethylation of homocysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM1-PM1](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) and [BRS2-FM1-PM2](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation). Using glutathione to limit lipid peroxidation belongs to [BRS3-FM2-PM5 — Lipid Peroxidation Control](/docs/biological-targets/brs3/fm2/brs3-fm2-pm5-lipid-peroxidation-control).

#### (Integration within BRS2)

Within [BRS2(FM2) — Transsulfuration & Redox Coupling](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-transsulfuration-redox-coupling), transsulfuration can supply cysteine and this reaction consumes it. Inadequacy of the shared methionine–cysteine pool can slow synthesis: whole-blood synthesis fell when both amino acids were removed [[3]](#pm-ref-3). That does not make selenium, riboflavin, or a clinical treatment part of the assembly step.

</div>
</div>
</div>

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

Human tracer studies show context-dependent substrate responsiveness. Removing methionine and cysteine together reduced whole-blood glutathione synthesis, whereas removing cysteine with methionine kept adequate did not reduce erythrocyte synthesis in young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) In older adults with lower baseline synthesis, combined N-acetylcysteine and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These contrasts support provision under defined conditions, not universal dietary cysteine limitation; blood-cell measurements do not establish neuronal synthesis or clinical benefit.

- [BRS3-FM2-PM5 — Lipid Peroxidation Control](/docs/biological-targets/brs3/fm2/brs3-fm2-pm5-lipid-peroxidation-control) — Glutathione made by these assembly steps can later be consumed when peroxides are reduced. ### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function.

- [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) — Converts homocysteine into cysteine that the first assembly step can use. This is upstream sulfur-amino-acid supply, not the ATP-dependent reactions that form glutathione.

---
title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
pm_id: BRS2-FM3-PM7
mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
parent_fm: BRS2(FM3)
parent_brs: BRS2
evidence_status: stage-2b-dietary-addressability
mechanistic_authoring_required: false
summary: >-
  Cells form phosphatidylcholine through distinct routes: hepatic PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine
  using SAMe, while the Kennedy pathway combines choline-derived phosphocholine with CTP and then
  diacylglycerol. Uridine can contribute upstream to nucleotide supply. These routes support membrane
  phospholipid provision; precursor availability does not establish that extra intake increases human membrane
  synthesis or improves cognition.
intervention_dominance: Diet-Supported
intervention_dominance_assessment:
  evidence_qualification:
    label: Diet-Supported
    rationale: >-
      The retained Diet-Supported qualification is supported by conditional PM-specific dietary influence; it
      does not establish comparative intervention dominance.
    scope_note: >-
      Conditional animal evidence concerns folate restriction and methyl-derived PC enrichment; it does not
      establish absolute PEMT flux, benefit above adequacy or cognitive benefit.
    routes:
      - group_id: '3.1'
        evidence_basis: intervention-effect
        intervention_effect: >-
          Eight-week folate restriction with labelled choline maintained reduced hepatic d3-PC enrichment and
          the product/precursor enrichment ratio in female mice.
        context: Female wild-type and Mthfr-heterozygous mice; the hepatic response was not demonstrated in males.
        limitations: >-
          Enrichment is not absolute PEMT flux. The restriction experiment does not establish supplementation
          benefit above adequacy, a human intake target or cognitive benefit.
        evidence_source:
          finding_ids:
            - PM7-F5
          citation_keys:
            - chew_folate_choline_2011
  principal_route_selection:
    disposition: established
    selected_groups:
      - '3.1'
    rationale: >-
      Dietary Requirements is the principal displayed route because the assessed folate-restriction
      intervention changed pathway-specific hepatic PC methyl enrichment, a mission-relevant endpoint. The
      measured conditional effect, rather than nutrient necessity or absence of competing levers, supports
      prominence. Precursor provision records explain the route but do not independently establish
      intervention responsiveness.
    comparative_limitations: >-
      Dietary prominence is supported within the studied animal context; it is not a head-to-head ranking
      against lifestyle or optimisation, a human intake target, or evidence of benefit from extra intake.
    assessments:
      - group_id: '3.1'
        relevance: >-
          PM7-F5 measures dietary methyl contribution to hepatic PC formation, directly relevant to the PEMT
          branch of this PM's mission.
        directness: >-
          Chew 2011 experimentally restricted folate for eight weeks with choline maintained; female mice had
          reduced labelled PC enrichment and a lower product/precursor enrichment ratio. This is dietary
          manipulation, not an inference from nutrient presence.
        extent: >-
          Hepatic d3-PC enrichment was 30% lower (P=0.017), with a lower d3-PC:d9-choline ratio (P=0.049).
          This supports substantial conditional dietary influence on the measured PEMT-related endpoint, not
          absolute flux or all PC synthesis. The hepatic response was not demonstrated in males, and no human
          or cognitive benefit is inferred.
intervention_breakdown: Food-State Leaning
timing_specific: 'No'
dose_sensitivity: >-
  Dietary methyl-donor provision is supported; increasing intake is not established to increase absolute PEMT
  activity or improve cognition.
kc_applicability_adjudications:
  - kc_id: BRS2(KC1)
    ikc_id: BRS2(KC1)
    arm_id: one-carbon-methyl-donor-pool
    applicability_proposition: >-
      Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine
      formation.
    disposition: established
    established_links:
      - >-
        KC1 defines folate, choline and betaine as a coherent remethylation donor pool; B12 remains an
        excluded cofactor.
      - >-
        Folate restriction with choline maintained reduced hepatic methyl-derived PC enrichment in female mice
        (PM7-F5).
      - >-
        Betaine restored reported PEMT-mediated production under ethanol-induced methylation imbalance
        (PM7-F5; abstract-level complementary evidence).
    inferred_links:
      - >-
        Absolute formation rate, universal donor limitation and human or cognitive benefit are not
        established.
    evidence_source:
      finding_ids:
        - PM7-F1
        - PM7-F5
      citation_keys:
        - chew_folate_choline_2011
        - kharbanda_betaine_pemt_2007
    rationale: >-
      Type D is met conditionally: named-donor restriction and complementary imbalance rescue connect this
      pool to pathway-specific formation. Enrichment is not absolute flux; a human or one end-to-end flux
      assay is not mandatory.
    applicability_mode: conditional-constraint
    legacy_applicability_mode: constrained-by
  - kc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    ikc_id: BRS2(KC2)
    arm_id: methionine-cysteine-sulfur-amino-acid-pool
    applicability_proposition: >-
      Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent
      phosphatidylcholine formation.
    disposition: unresolved
    established_links:
      - >-
        Dietary methionine supplies the upstream MAT/SAM route used by PEMT (PM7-F1/F6). This supported chain
        is not rejected for being upstream.
      - >-
        Shimada 2003 Table 4 separates methionine-associated phospholipid changes from cystine-associated
        growth rescue with choline held constant; PC:PE and SAM concentrations are not PEMT flux.
      - >-
        Asiriwardhana 2025 Figure 4C measures dietary methionine-dependent methyl incorporation into hepatic
        PC in neonatal piglets; cysteine was held constant. This closes the concentration-only endpoint gap.
      - >-
        Robinson 2016 primary abstract reports higher hepatic PC synthesis and lower creatine synthesis after
        donor removal with methionine restricted in both groups. Allocation is context-dependent, not uniform
        suppression.
      - >-
        Sugiyama 1995 primary abstract reports that eritadenine did not directly inhibit PEMT in the assay;
        the 1998 inhibitor comparison is not a selective PEMT blockade.
      - >-
        Cano 2011 indexed primary results and prior appraisal support altered PEMT activity after MAT1A
        deletion. Genetic SAM-production impairment is not dietary sulfur-pool inadequacy.
    inferred_links:
      - >-
        Whether methionine–cysteine pool availability creates a separately supported allocation, competition
        or other constraint on PEMT beyond the documented methionine-to-SAM provision job. Cysteine
        compensation and the relevant context remain unestablished for this proposition.
    evidence_source:
      finding_ids:
        - PM7-F1
        - PM7-F6
      citation_keys:
        - sugiyama_methionine_pe_1998
        - shimada_methionine_desaturase_2003
        - cano_mat1a_vldl_2011
        - sugiyama_eritadenine_phospholipid_1995
        - robinson_methyl_donors_partitioning_2016
        - asiriwardhana_methionine_transmethylation_2025
    rationale: >-
      Retain the specified conditional-constraint proposition unresolved, while recognising supported upstream
      methionine provision and measured nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC. No human,
      universal deficiency or absolute-flux gate is imposed. Provision evidence does not by itself establish a
      distinct shared sulfur-pool bottleneck; donor restriction can redistribute synthesis rather than lower
      PC synthesis.
    evidence_gap: >-
      Evidence linking the named methionine–cysteine pool, including cysteine compensation where relevant, to
      a constraint beyond methionine/SAM provision in a specified context. Sugiyama 1998 full methods and Cano
      2011 full assay methods remain inaccessible in this pass; neither access gap is treated as proof of
      non-applicability.
    review_record: system/brs2-fm3-pm7-kc2-focused-reassessment.md

scientific_findings_intro: >-
  Enzyme localisation, mutagenesis and kinetic evidence establishes PEMT-mediated phosphatidylcholine
  formation and regulation by its substrates and methyl-transfer product. [[7]](#pm-ref-7) [[8]](#pm-ref-8)
  [[9]](#pm-ref-9) Donor restriction/rescue and upstream perturbation studies support bounded dependence, with
  experimental contexts limiting extrapolation. [[11]](#pm-ref-11) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) [[15]](#pm-ref-15) Human
  tracing identifies methyl-derived phosphatidylcholine separately from intact-headgroup incorporation,
  supporting provision without establishing indispensable dependence, increased absolute hepatic flux or brain
  benefit. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) Kennedy-pathway studies add a separate nucleotide-provision chain: uridine
  increased CDP-choline formation in rat slices, and oral UMP increased brain precursor pools in gerbils.
  [[19]](#pm-ref-19) [[20]](#pm-ref-20) Human MRS provides connected precursor-pool evidence rather than proof
  of PC synthesis or benefit. [[21]](#pm-ref-21) A longer gerbil study measured PC abundance after dietary
  UMP, a stronger lipid endpoint than precursor pools, but not a human flux or benefit result.
  [[22]](#pm-ref-22)
scientific_findings:
  - id: PM7-F1
    finding_label: PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: true
    finding_summary: >-
      In the liver, phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT) adds three methyl groups from
      S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) to phosphatidylethanolamine and releases phosphatidylcholine. Magnesium is
      not a cofactor of this reaction. The CDP-choline route is a separate way to make phosphatidylcholine.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      Phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe are the substrates of the methylation. Choline feeds the parallel
      route, and animals that lack PEMT need dietary choline. That does not make choline a substrate of this
      methylation, and it does not make supplemental SAMe or magnesium a requirement of it.
    finding_statement: >-
      Hepatic PEMT converts phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine by three sequential SAMe-dependent
      methyl transfers. The reaction substrates are phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe. Magnesium is not an
      established cofactor of this reaction, and the CDP-choline pathway is a parallel route outside it.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      Human liver enzyme localisation, SAMe-binding mutagenesis and a physiological review agree on the
      reaction boundary. PEMT in the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes of liver uses
      SAMe to methylate phosphatidylethanolamine in three steps, through phosphatidylmonomethylethanolamine
      and phosphatidyldimethylethanolamine, to phosphatidylcholine. Conserved residues are required for SAMe
      binding and activity. Mice that lack PEMT tolerate a normal diet, but a choline-deficient diet causes
      liver failure within days because the CDP-choline route is then unavailable as well. None of these
      sources names magnesium as a PEMT cofactor.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The enzyme evidence is recombinant protein and a review of knockout mice, not a human dietary flux
      study. Absence of magnesium from the reaction description rejects the claim that magnesium is a PEMT
      cofactor; it does not test every buffer condition in the older assay literature. The choline-deficient
      knockout result shows that choline supports a parallel route. It does not show that choline is a PEMT
      substrate or that choline intake increases this methylation.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Shields et al. (2003) — topography
        citation_key: shields_pemt_topography_2003
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#shields_pemt_topography_2003
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Human liver PEMT activity localises to the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated
          membranes and catalyses three SAMe-dependent methylations of phosphatidylethanolamine.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Endoproteinase-protection mapping of epitope-tagged human PEMT and biochemical localisation in
            human liver.
          population: >-
            Human liver fractions and recombinant protein. No dietary intervention and no human participants
            in a feeding study.
          result: >-
            Methyltransferase activity localised primarily to the endoplasmic reticulum and
            mitochondria-associated membranes. The enzyme spans the membrane four times. S-adenosylmethionine
            is the methyl donor for three sequential methylations.
          effect_magnitude: No dietary dose or in-vivo flux estimate.
          evidence_summary: 'Direct description of the human hepatic reaction, its localisation and its methyl donor.'
          limitations: Topography and localisation do not show that ordinary diet changes PEMT rate.
      - label: Shields et al. (2003) — SAMe binding
        citation_key: shields_pemt_adomet_2003
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#shields_pemt_adomet_2003
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Conserved residues in human PEMT are required for S-adenosylmethionine binding and for enzyme
          activity.
        assessment:
          study: >-
            Site-directed mutagenesis of predicted S-adenosylmethionine-binding motifs in recombinant human
            PEMT, with binding measurements.
          population: Recombinant human PEMT. No animals or human participants.
          result: >-
            Gly100 and Glu180 were essential for S-adenosylmethionine binding. Conservative changes at Gly98
            and Glu181 raised the reported binding parameter relative to unmodified enzyme. The abstract
            describes three sequential methylations of phosphatidylethanolamine and names
            S-adenosylhomocysteine as a product.
          effect_magnitude: >-
            The paper reports the binding comparison as 303.1 pmol for unmodified enzyme, 400 pmol after the
            Gly98 change and 666.7 pmol after the Glu181 change. These are not dietary doses.
          evidence_summary: Direct evidence that SAMe binding is required for human PEMT activity.
          limitations: >-
            A recombinant binding study does not show that supplemental SAMe increases hepatic
            phosphatidylcholine formation in people.
      - label: Vance (2014)
        citation_key: vance_phospholipid_2014
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#vance_phospholipid_2014
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine using AdoMet. Supply of AdoMet, phosphatidylethanolamine
          and the product AdoHcy can regulate activity. Loss of PEMT plus a choline-deficient diet causes
          rapid liver failure in mice.
        assessment:
          study: 'Narrative review of PEMT localisation, regulation and knockout-mouse physiology.'
          population: >-
            Review, including Pemt knockout mice fed chow or a choline-deficient diet. Not a human enzyme-rate
            trial.
          result: >-
            PEMT is a liver endoplasmic-reticulum and mitochondria-associated-membrane enzyme. Substrate
            supply and product AdoHcy can regulate it. Knockout mice have a mild phenotype on chow. On a
            choline-deficient diet they develop steatohepatitis and liver failure after 3 days, with a lower
            phosphatidylcholine to phosphatidylethanolamine ratio and leakage from hepatocyte membranes.
          effect_magnitude: Liver failure by 3 days in Pemt knockout mice fed a choline-deficient diet. No human PEMT flux.
          evidence_summary: >-
            Physiological boundary for the substrates, product regulation and the parallel choline-dependent
            route.
          limitations: >-
            Review synthesis. The knockout diet result removes PEMT and dietary choline together. It does not
            show that choline is methylated by PEMT.
    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        Vance (2014) is also primary evidence in PM7-F2 for the separate claim that S-adenosylhomocysteine can
        regulate activity. It is not a second independent demonstration of the methyl-transfer chemistry.
    connected_supportive_evidence:
      - label: Ridgway and Vance (1988)
        citation_key: ridgway_pemt_kinetics_1988
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#ridgway_pemt_kinetics_1988
        data_level: Cellular / Molecular
        why_relevant: >-
          Purified rat-liver kinetics place phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe in an ordered mechanism and
          release S-adenosylhomocysteine after methyl transfer.
        why_excluded: >-
          The primary use of this paper is the product-regulation proposition in PM7-F2. It is cited here only
          to confirm the same substrates.
  - id: PM7-F2
    finding_label: S-adenosylhomocysteine can regulate PEMT
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: >-
      Each methyl transfer releases S-adenosylhomocysteine. The supply of that product can regulate PEMT
      activity. These sources do not show that a high homocysteine concentration itself was measured as a PEMT
      inhibitor.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      Product regulation is part of the reaction. It is not evidence that lowering homocysteine with B
      vitamins changes the rate of this methylation in people.
    finding_statement: >-
      S-adenosylhomocysteine, the product released after each PEMT methyl transfer, can regulate PEMT
      activity. The attached and retrieved sources do not demonstrate that elevated homocysteine itself
      inhibits human PEMT.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      The physiological review states that the product AdoHcy, together with the substrates AdoMet and
      phosphatidylethanolamine, can regulate PEMT. Purified rat-liver kinetics fit an ordered mechanism in
      which the phospholipid binds first, S-adenosylmethionine then binds, the methyl group is transferred and
      S-adenosylhomocysteine is released. Product-inhibition patterns were part of that kinetic analysis.
      Neither source reports a human experiment in which homocysteine concentration was the inhibitor tested
      against PEMT.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      Regulation is stated in a review and inferred from product release and product-inhibition patterns in
      purified enzyme. The kinetic abstract does not give an S-adenosylhomocysteine inhibition constant.
      Homocysteine and S-adenosylhomocysteine are not interchangeable measurements. No human PEMT rate under
      raised homocysteine was assessed.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Vance (2014)
        citation_key: vance_phospholipid_2014
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#vance_phospholipid_2014
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-

## BRS2-3-7 - Phosphatidylcholine Formation

(PEMT methylation and Kennedy-pathway phosphatidylcholine synthesis)

## 1. Mission, Objective & Biological Context

### Mission

Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.



### Overview

Cells form phosphatidylcholine through distinct routes: hepatic PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine using SAMe, while the Kennedy pathway combines choline-derived phosphocholine with CTP and then diacylglycerol. Uridine can contribute upstream to nucleotide supply. These routes support membrane phospholipid provision; precursor availability does not establish that extra intake increases human membrane synthesis or improves cognition. [[19]](#pm-ref-19) [[20]](#pm-ref-20) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)

- **Benefits:** PC formation supplies a major membrane phospholipid. PEMT/choline-route loss in mice demonstrates the importance of maintaining hepatic PC provision; the new uridine evidence measures precursor formation, not a clinical benefit. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)
- **Implementation Notes:** Choline and phosphatidylcholine can supply the existing methyl-donor provision route. Uridine adds a supported nucleotide-precursor route, with no established ordinary-food dose or human PC-flux benefit. [[20]](#pm-ref-20) [[21]](#pm-ref-21)
- **Biological Relevance:** Only the PEMT branch directly couples methylation to membrane chemistry in the parent FM. Kennedy synthesis is a parallel PC-forming route; brain DHA delivery and incorporation remain separate downstream jobs. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

Phosphatidylcholine formation through distinct PEMT and Kennedy routes; S-adenosylhomocysteine production confined to PEMT methyl transfer. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

PC formation has two distinct routes. Hepatic PEMT uses SAMe to methylate phosphatidylethanolamine. The Kennedy pathway builds PC using choline, CTP and diacylglycerol; uridine can contribute to its nucleotide supply. Neither route alone establishes brain DHA uptake or cognitive benefit. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

<div class="brs-fm-hub-item" data-brs-fm-hub>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-shell">
<button type="button" class="brs-fm-hub-summary" aria-expanded="false">
<span class="brs-fm-hub-chevron" aria-hidden="true"></span>
<strong>Phosphatidylcholine formation — mechanistic detail</strong>
</button>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-panel" hidden>

#### (Three methyl transfers)

Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT) in human liver sits mainly in the endoplasmic reticulum and in the membranes where mitochondria meet that reticulum. It methylates phosphatidylethanolamine (a phospholipid already in the membrane) three times. The methyl groups come from S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe, the methyl-group donor). The intermediates are phosphatidylmonomethylethanolamine and phosphatidyldimethylethanolamine. The phospholipid product is phosphatidylcholine, and each transfer releases S-adenosylhomocysteine [Shields et al. (2003) [[7]](#pm-ref-7); Shields et al. (2003) [[8]](#pm-ref-8)].

#### (What the reaction uses)

The substrates are phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe. Conserved amino acids in the human enzyme are required for SAMe binding and for activity [Shields et al. (2003) [[8]](#pm-ref-8)]. Purified rat-liver enzyme follows an ordered sequence: the phospholipid binds, SAMe binds, the methyl group moves, and S-adenosylhomocysteine leaves [Ridgway and Vance (1988) [[9]](#pm-ref-9)]. The supply of those substrates, and of S-adenosylhomocysteine, can regulate activity [Vance (2014) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)]. Magnesium is not part of this reaction. It helps the upstream enzyme that makes SAMe. It is not a cofactor shown for PEMT.

SAMe used here is produced by methionine adenosyltransferase in [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). Needing that methyl donor does not make a SAMe supplement the substrate, and it does not show that more SAMe intake speeds these methylations.

#### (Kennedy-pathway PC formation)

Choline is phosphorylated to phosphocholine. CTP then supplies the nucleotide used to form CDP-choline; transfer of its phosphocholine group to diacylglycerol forms PC. This route does not consume SAMe methyl groups. Uridine can enter nucleotide metabolism upstream of CTP. [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

In rat brain slices, uridine increased CDP-choline formation without reducing measured acetylcholine release. Oral UMP increased brain uridine, UTP, CTP and CDP-choline in gerbils. Those are provision and precursor endpoints, not measurements of absolute human PC synthesis. [[19]](#pm-ref-19) [[20]](#pm-ref-20) In a four-week gerbil study, dietary UMP also increased measured PC abundance on a choline-containing diet (Table 1A); this was not a synthesis-flux measurement. [[22]](#pm-ref-22) Human uridine administration changed phosphomonoester signals on phosphorus MRS; these signals do not establish membrane accretion or cognition. [[21]](#pm-ref-21)

#### (Boundaries of the mechanism)

The CDP-choline pathway, also called the Kennedy pathway, builds phosphatidylcholine from choline by different reactions. Mice that lack PEMT cope on an ordinary diet. The same mice develop liver failure within three days if the diet also lacks choline, because both routes are then missing. The liver phosphatidylcholine to phosphatidylethanolamine ratio falls and hepatocyte membranes leak [Vance (2014) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)]. Choline therefore supports the parallel route. It is not the molecule PEMT methylates.

Blood–brain transport of DHA and its uptake into neuronal membranes are later steps, described under [BRS1-FM3-PM7 — Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm3/brs1-fm3-pm7-neuronal-membrane-dha-incorporation). A piglet comparison of phospholipid-bound and triglyceride-bound DHA measured brain accretion, and the liver was labelled most heavily [Liu et al. (2014) [[3]](#pm-ref-3)]. A human trial measured DHA in cerebrospinal fluid after supplements, while both groups also took B vitamins, and cognitive scores did not differ [Arellanes et al. (2020) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)]. Neither study measured how fast PEMT works.

In mild cognitive impairment, B vitamins were linked with slower cognitive decline when omega-3 status was higher [Oulhaj et al. (2016) [[4]](#pm-ref-4)]. That is a clinical interaction. It is not an assay of this methylation. Diet reviews in ADHD and choline reviews in neurodevelopment likewise do not measure the enzyme [Millichap and Yee (2012) [[5]](#pm-ref-5); Derbyshire and Maes (2023) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)].

#### (Integration within BRS2)

Within [BRS2(FM3) — Methylation–Membrane Coupling](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-methylation-membrane-coupling), this is the methylation that turns phosphatidylethanolamine into phosphatidylcholine. [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) can regenerate methionine that later becomes SAMe. That is earlier than the methyl transfers. [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis) is the reaction that supplies the SAMe used here. Methionine supplies that SAMe upstream. Neonatal piglet tracing shows dietary methionine-dependent methyl incorporation into hepatic PC [[18]](#pm-ref-18). This supports provision; a distinct methionine–cysteine pool constraint remains unresolved (PM7-F6). Neuronal DHA incorporation remains the downstream step in [BRS1-FM3-PM7 — Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm3/brs1-fm3-pm7-neuronal-membrane-dha-incorporation).

[BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation)
↓
[BRS2-FM3-PM7 — Phosphatidylcholine Formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation)
↓
[BRS1-FM3-PM7 — Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm3/brs1-fm3-pm7-neuronal-membrane-dha-incorporation)

### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships

Primary Mechanisms in other Biological Regulatory Systems that directly interact with, constrain or support this mechanism.

- [BRS1-FM3-PM7 — Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm3/brs1-fm3-pm7-neuronal-membrane-dha-incorporation) — Hepatic methylation produces phosphatidylcholine from phosphatidylethanolamine. Later blood–brain transport of DHA and its uptake into neuronal membranes are a downstream delivery step, not this methyl transfer.

### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function.

- [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) — Choline-derived betaine contributes methyl groups through homocysteine remethylation to methionine and subsequent SAMe synthesis. This upstream chain supports methyl-group provision to PEMT (PM7-F7).

- [BRS2-FM1-PM3 - SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis) — Methionine adenosyltransferase produces the S-adenosylmethionine consumed in each phosphatidylethanolamine methylation. That is upstream methyl-donor supply, not the methylation reaction itself.

## 7. Phenome Connections

These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

### Overview

NAD⁺ helps cells release energy from nutrients and supports enzymes involved in maintenance and repair. Cells must continually recycle and replenish this molecule to keep those functions available. This PM focuses on maintaining that cellular resource. Dietary vitamin B3 forms and tryptophan provide building material, while exercise can influence part of the recycling machinery. Supporting normal availability is different from assuming that raising NAD⁺ improves cognition or wellbeing. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)

- **Benefits:** Maintaining NAD⁺ supports energy metabolism and cellular repair—functions needed for healthy tissue function. This explains the value of the mechanism, rather than demonstrating a benefit from extra intake. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[3]](#pm-ref-3)
- **Implementation Notes:** The dietary disclosures identify the specific vitamin B3 forms and tryptophan that supply this pool. Aerobic or resistance training increased a recycling enzyme in human muscle; high-dose niacin evidence comes from mitochondrial disease and does not establish a routine supplement regimen. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)
- **Biological Relevance:** This resource connects mitochondrial energy metabolism with cellular maintenance and repair. It also interacts with biological timing mechanisms, linking energy regulation with the body’s daily rhythms. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

NAD⁺ accepts electrons to form NADH, which can be oxidised back to NAD⁺ [Covarrubias et al. (2021) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)]. Separately, synthesis and salvage replenish the pool when consuming enzymes break the molecule down [Chang and Guarente (2014) [[3]](#pm-ref-3)]. Nicotinamide salvage, the nicotinic-acid route and hepatic tryptophan conversion are major pathways [Covarrubias et al. (2021) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)]. In mice, the clock controls the salvage enzyme NAMPT [Ramsey et al. (2009) [[4]](#pm-ref-4)]. High-dose niacin raised NAD⁺ in mitochondrial myopathy [Pirinen et al. (2020) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)]. Training raised the muscle enzyme, not measured NAD⁺ [de Guia et al. (2019) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)].

### Mechanism and measurement boundaries

This PM includes NAD⁺ replenishment, redox use and enzymatic consumption. Electron transport and the creatine buffer are distinct mechanisms. [[1]](#pm-ref-1)

The precursor pathways are supported by reviewed mechanistic evidence. The high-dose niacin study involved five adults with mitochondrial myopathy; exercise measured muscle NAMPT protein, not NAD⁺ concentration or brain function. These endpoints do not establish improved cognitive energy or recovery. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

NAD⁺ and NADH interconvert in dehydrogenase reactions. Separately, synthesis and salvage replenish the pool when consuming enzymes break NAD⁺ down. Nicotinamide salvage, the nicotinic-acid route and hepatic tryptophan conversion are major pathways, not every precursor entry. The findings separate that chemistry from a high-dose niacin study in mitochondrial myopathy, from a muscle-enzyme response to training, and from the absence of an NAD⁺ measurement in the ADHD papers.

### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships

- [BRS-X(Circadian-FM1) — Light and Feeding Zeitgeber Entrainment](/docs/biological-targets/brs-x/circadian/fm1/brs-x-circadian-fm1-zeitgeber-entrainment) — molecular clocks regulate NAMPT-dependent NAD⁺ biosynthesis in mice and cells ([Ramsey et al., 2009](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#ramsey_circadian_2009)). This supports clock–metabolic feedback, without establishing that a light or meal schedule changes human NAD⁺ availability. NAD⁺ metabolism retains its BRS4 owner.

Primary Mechanisms in other Biological Regulatory Systems that directly interact with, constrain or support this mechanism.

- [BRS2-FM1-PM4 - Methionine Cycle Flux](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm4-methionine-cycle-flux) — One-carbon reactions use redox cofactors. No assessed study shows that this turnover changes how much NAD⁺ cells hold.
- [BRS6-FM1-PM2 - Glycaemic Variability Regulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation) — Carbohydrate oxidation reduces NAD⁺ to NADH. Control of glucose swings is a separate process, and no assessed study shows that those swings change NAD⁺ availability.

### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function.

- [BRS4-FM1-PM1 - Electron Transport Chain Function](/docs/biological-targets/brs4/fm1/brs4-fm1-pm1-electron-transport-chain-function) — NADH made from this pool is what complex I oxidises. The respiratory complexes are a separate mechanism, and niacin precursors belong with this supply.
- [BRS4-FM1-PM3 - Creatine–Phosphocreatine Energy Buffering](/docs/biological-targets/brs4/fm1/brs4-fm1-pm3-creatine-phosphocreatine-buffer) — Oxidative energy production can supply ATP that this buffer stores and releases. No assessed study shows a serial path from this NAD⁺ pool through the respiratory complexes into that buffer.

title: Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity

mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.
summary: >-
  The gut lining is a selective gate. Tight junctions, the seals between its cells, control which materials
  pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange.
  Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models;
  glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological
  routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement.

scientific_findings_intro: >-
  Butyrate and zinc experiments directly interrogate epithelial junction function. Retinoids influence
  differentiation and permeability, but their direction depends on the model. A selected postinfectious IBS
  trial found a glutamine response; heterogeneous supplementation evidence does not support a general regimen.
  Microbiota associations do not establish a barrier-to-cognition effect. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)
  [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[6]](#pm-ref-6) Alcohol studies identify a context-specific barrier
  stressor and recovery relationship; carotenoid absorption supports upstream delivery, and fermented-milk
  findings remain preparation- and population-specific.
scientific_findings:
  - id: PM1-F1
    finding_label: Tight junctions govern selective paracellular permeability
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: >-
      Intestinal epithelial tight junctions form regulated pore and leak pathways that determine selective
      paracellular passage.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports the PM boundary around epithelial gate function. Downstream microbial-product containment
      and systemic inflammation remain outside it.
    finding_statement: >-
      Intestinal tight-junction structure and regulation determine selective paracellular permeability, while
      epithelial injury can create a distinct unrestricted permeability pathway.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      An authoritative mechanistic review distinguishes tight-junction-dependent pore and leak pathways from
      unrestricted flux caused by epithelial damage. In a mouse pneumonia model, increased permeability and
      claudin-2 were attenuated by oral LGG, providing intervention evidence that barrier permeability and
      junction-associated biology can move together under pathological conditions.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The review establishes mechanism rather than dietary responsiveness. The LGG experiment was performed in
      young mice with experimental Pseudomonas pneumonia, not in healthy humans, and does not establish a
      generic fermented-food effect.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Chanez-Paredes and Turner (2023)
        citation_key: chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Tight junctions define size- and charge-selective pore and leak pathways; epithelial damage produces
          a separate unrestricted pathway.
      - label: Khailova et al. (2017)
        citation_key: khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        data_level: Animal Data
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Oral LGG attenuated pneumonia-induced intestinal permeability and claudin-2 elevation and supported
          mucin expression in mice.
  - id: PM1-F2
    finding_label: Butyrate can support epithelial tight-junction assembly
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: Microbial fermentation products, especially butyrate, can act directly on epithelial barrier biology.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports a Direct butyrate relationship and a Derived fermentable-fibre provision relationship,
      with microbiota and fibre-specific limitations.
    finding_statement: >-
      Butyrate can function as an epithelial metabolic substrate and promote intestinal tight-junction
      assembly, while fermentable dietary fibre lies upstream as microbial substrate provision for
      short-chain-fatty-acid production.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In Caco-2 monolayers, physiological butyrate increased transepithelial resistance, reduced inulin
      permeability and accelerated tight-junction assembly alongside AMPK activation. A broader review links
      microbial fermentation of dietary substrates to short-chain-fatty-acid production and intestinal barrier
      effects.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The direct assembly experiment is an immortalised epithelial-cell model. Fibre-to-butyrate conversion
      varies by fibre structure and microbial ecology, and neither source establishes a universal human intake
      threshold, a generic effect of all fibre, or oral butyrate as necessary treatment.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Peng et al. (2009)
        citation_key: peng_butyrate_2009
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#peng_butyrate_2009
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Butyrate increased barrier resistance, reduced inulin permeability and accelerated tight-junction
          assembly in Caco-2 monolayers.
      - label: Silva et al. (2020)
        citation_key: silva_role_2020
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#silva_role_2020
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          The review links microbial fermentation-derived short-chain fatty acids with epithelial barrier and
          gut-brain communication mechanisms.
  - id: PM1-F3
    finding_label: Barrier markers and attention-related symptoms are associated, not causal
    presentation: phenome-relationship
    primary_phenome: Focus / Attention Stability
    finding_summary: >-
      One small cross-sectional ADHD study linked serum zonulin with hyperactivity, but it did not establish a
      causal tight-junction-to-attention pathway.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      The evidence is compatible with the proposed relationship but is too indirect to show that changing PM1
      changes attention stability.
    finding_statement: >-
      Current human evidence provides only indirect observational support for a relationship between
      intestinal barrier biology and attention-related symptoms.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In children with ADHD, serum zonulin was independently associated with hyperactivity and social-function
      scores. A separate microbiota study found lower Faecalibacterium abundance associated with parent-rated
      ADHD symptoms, but it did not measure barrier function. Together these studies support hypothesis
      generation, not a PM1-specific causal relationship.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      Both studies are small and cross-sectional. Serum zonulin is an indirect permeability marker; neither
      study manipulated or directly quantified tight-junction integrity, and neither demonstrates that PM1
      changes attention outcomes.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Özyurt et al. (2018)
        citation_key: ozyurt_increased_2018
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#ozyurt_increased_2018
        data_level: Human Study
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Higher serum zonulin was independently associated with greater hyperactivity and social impairment
          in children with ADHD.
      - label: Jiang et al. (2018)
        citation_key: jiang_gut_2018
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#jiang_gut_2018
        data_level: Human Study
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Lower Faecalibacterium abundance was associated with parent-rated ADHD symptoms, but permeability
          and tight-junction function were not measured.
    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        The two studies address different proxies and cannot be treated as independent replications of a PM1 →
        attention relationship.
    fm_rollup: false
  - id: PM1-F4
    finding_label: Direct evidence for an Emotional Regulation relationship is absent
    presentation: phenome-relationship
    primary_phenome: Emotional Regulation
    finding_summary: The attached human study does not measure PM1 or emotional regulation.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      Emotional Regulation remains a framework-level hypothesis rather than an evidence-established PM1
      relationship.
    finding_statement: >-
      The bounded evidence assessment does not establish that gut tight-junction integrity modulates Emotional
      Regulation.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      Jiang et al. measured faecal microbiota composition and parent-rated ADHD symptoms. It did not measure
      intestinal permeability, tight-junction function or emotional-regulation outcomes, so it cannot directly
      support the current PM1 → Emotional Regulation proposition.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      This is an evidence-gap adjudication, not evidence that no biological relationship exists. Targeted
      barrier measures and emotional-regulation outcomes would be needed to test the proposition.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Jiang et al. (2018)
        citation_key: jiang_gut_2018
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#jiang_gut_2018
        data_level: Human Study
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          The study reported microbiota-composition associations with ADHD symptoms but did not measure either

    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        Jiang et al. is also assessed in PM1-F3 because the same attached study was previously used for both

    title: Resistant Starch–Derived Butyrate and Tight-Junction Regulation

      butyrate production and local exposure.
    source_pm: BRS5-FM2-PM5
    target_pm: BRS5-FM1-PM1
    proposed_direction: BRS5-FM2-PM5 → BRS5-FM1-PM1

    rationale: >-
      Selected resistant-starch preparations support microbial butyrate production, and direct butyrate
      exposure can influence epithelial junction assembly. These separate observations motivate testing the
      joined dietary pathway; they do not establish it. The proposed five-link chain is: (1) dietary
      resistant-starch substrate reaches a capable microbial community; (2) utilisation and cross-feeding
      generate a context-dependent butyrate pool; (3) luminal butyrate becomes available to and is taken up by
      the epithelium; (4) cellular butyrate exposure engages pathways such as AMPK-related tight-junction
      assembly; (5) local engagement would produce a demonstrable paracellular tight-junction functional
      effect in the relevant host context. Evidence for separate links does not establish the complete chain.
      Moreau’s increased uptake followed healing; Peng’s cellular mechanism and the bounded human
      null/transcellular results must not be joined into an established dietary effect.

## BRS5-1-1 - Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity


## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported. Dietary inputs are the principal group displayed here, within the study-specific boundaries. Comparative dominance is not established.

### Overview

The gut lining is a selective gate. Tight junctions, the seals between its cells, control which materials pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange. Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models; glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

- **Benefits:** Selective permeability helps limit inappropriate passage across the gut lining; symptom benefits from supplementation are specific to the populations studied.
- **Implementation Notes:** Fermentable substrates can supply microbial butyrate. Nutrient adequacy differs from extra-intake benefit; the glutamine trial concerned postinfectious diarrhoea-predominant IBS with confirmed hyperpermeability.
- **Biological Relevance:** This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

↑ tight-junction strength; ↓ permeability

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Cellular zinc supports junction-protein maintenance; retinoic acid influences epithelial differentiation and selective permeability. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Biological process

The zinc result supports a bounded cellular requirement. Retinoid biology cannot be simplified to lower permeability in every context. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Mechanism Boundary

This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

#### Integration

This PM contributes its specific process to its parent FM. Shared inputs do not merge distinct jobs or prove an integrated clinical outcome.

## BRS5-2-6 - Polyphenol Biotransformation & Mitochondrial-Relevant Metabolite Generation


## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.

**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported. Dietary inputs are the principal group displayed here, within the study-specific boundaries. Comparative dominance is not established.

### Overview

Gut microbes can convert some dietary polyphenols into different metabolites. Ellagitannins release ellagic acid, from which cooperating microbes can form urolithins. Not everyone completes this conversion to urolithin A. Understanding that variability separates microbial processing from taking the finished metabolite as a supplement. [[5]](#pm-ref-5)

- **Benefits:** Microbial conversion can make metabolites available for downstream biology. Human mitochondrial findings after direct urolithin A administration do not prove benefit from foods or improved microbial conversion.
- **Implementation Notes:** Ellagic acid and its ellagitannin precursors provide the studied route’s substrate. Food matrix and microbial conversion capacity matter; direct urolithin A bypasses this mechanism.
- **Biological Relevance:** Do not generalise the ellagic-acid route to all polyphenols, tea, cocoa or plant diversity. Downstream mitophagy evidence must retain its administered-metabolite exposure.

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

- Ellagic acid conversion requires microbial activity; particular species perform intermediate steps, and human completion varies. [[5]](#pm-ref-5)
- Administered urolithin A has downstream mitochondrial and experimental cognition findings. [[1]](#pm-ref-1)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Ellagic acid conversion requires microbial activity; particular species perform intermediate steps, and human completion varies. [[5]](#pm-ref-5)

#### Biological process

Ellagic acid and ellagitannin provision support the route. A finished-metabolite supplement does not assess that conversion. [[5]](#pm-ref-5)

#### Mechanism Boundary

Do not generalise the ellagic-acid route to all polyphenols, tea, cocoa or plant diversity. Downstream mitophagy evidence must retain its administered-metabolite exposure.

#### Integration

This PM contributes its specific process to its parent FM. Shared inputs do not merge distinct jobs or prove an integrated clinical outcome.

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

Culture studies identify partial ellagic-acid conversion by particular bacteria. Human pomegranate exposure shows substantial variation in urolithin A generation. Direct urolithin A studies preserve downstream evidence but bypass the microbial step. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[3]](#pm-ref-3)
